summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the supplier/ERP data drops, find what Soony's launch plan misses, and build a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier emails, approvals) plus the hand-in materials by Sunday 12:00.
summary.outcome: Found that the plan said 'all ok' while Collector's and Standard editions would miss Sunday 20:00 (80,000 vs 8,000 art-book overbooking, failed statue lot, stuck container, offloaded game cards). Built and pushed a working app (Today/Launch/routines/approval loop, 317 tests, 23 commits on `jonas/today-flow`), and started README and demo script plus a Launch-for-Maren change.

repo: Confidential portal data lives only in the gitignored `data/` folder; `.env` is gitignored and `.env.example` is committed, with the portal token empty.
The team workflow uses `CLAUDE.md` and `PROGRESS.md`; claim tasks with a Now line in `PROGRESS.md` before coding.

The portal API has three endpoints: files list, single file, archive.zip. It has no webhook or notification endpoint, so you poll and compare SHA-256 checksums. Existing files are replaced under the same name.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions that only read files log 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint'.

Routine bug: option matching searched the literal text 'make po,rev' instead of 'make po' AND 'rev'; the stored routine had to be regenerated. Routines also mark cases as seen on the first run, so they will not retry them.
Prepared routine steps must expire when their case is decided, and the same step for the same case must be deduped across routines; otherwise the UI shows stale 'not an open card' steps.
Push notifications go to every subscribed device, with no per-person targeting; the `/ok/<token>` approval page needs no password because `basic_auth.py` lets valid links through.
`ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds>` (off by default) auto-approves a passed-on escalation, labelled 'simulated for the demo'; `ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK` is empty so nothing reaches Teams.
workflow: A one-time subagent cross-check of all 200 order confirmations and 59 scans found the data discrepancies faster than reading them manually.

Verify UI fixes in a real browser (press J seven times, click a decided row, measure scroll) rather than relying on typecheck alone; this caught a scroll-reset bug that was caused by two rows both being marked selected.
Delegating UI/UX and feature builds to subagents while committing in between worked, but uncommitted subagent output has to be committed before touching the same files again.
Keep sensitive data and the portal login out of shared docs and artifacts.

friction: The token was initially empty, which blocked data access until the user supplied it.

The transcript shows several UX regressions that had to be fixed in sequence: the left list did not scroll, picking a decided case reset the scroll, waiting steps were missing from the sidebar, and 'Do all 4' failed on stale steps.
Routine toggles sometimes seemed to do nothing ('not run yet'), and the routine's first run failed because of the option-matching bug.
Internal messages and escalations were only recorded and went nowhere, while the screen claimed 'DC site lead has it now'.
PackRight received two more rev C requests after already answering, and an email to one address bounced because the address does not exist.
Duplicate routines caused double-prepared Hamburg count questions.

Send a better follow-up to PackRight (rev C file and change notice, ask how much is unprinted) and a note to Hwaseong; resolve the Pulse note and the message to Lucas.
